summary: DSS (Decision-Support System) upgrade — backend contract testing complete. Validated Insight Confidence Engine, DSS guardrails (alert suppression for Medium/Low), data_quality classification/exclusion, probabilistic alert wording, and multi-tenant boundary. 47/47 tests pass: 27 pre-existing pure-function unit tests (test_dss_confidence.py 16 + test_price_intelligence_milestone4.py 11) + 20 new HTTP contract tests in test_dss_price_intelligence.py. Every products-list item exposes confidence{score,level,components,weights,explanation}, recommendation{level,actionable,label,headline,detail,action,tags}, and data_quality{good,fair,poor}. Weights are exactly recency=0.30, observations=0.25, identity=0.25, unit=0.20, and level mapping (High≥0.80, Medium 0.60–0.79, Low<0.60) is enforced per item. Poor-quality records surface in raw history (with data_quality_flag) but are correctly excluded from stats/trend/alert/vendor comparisons; the poor-only product (Ground Beef 80/20) returns confidence=low, stats.observations=0, alert=null, tags={review_suggested,data_thin}, action=null, and /vendors returns 404. Alerts endpoint and dashboard smart_alerts only surface confidence_level=='high' alerts. Alert/message wording is probabilistic ('High likelihood…' — no 'overpaying'). Backfill tags every inserted record with data_quality_flag.

critical_code_review_comments: evaluate_alert DSS gate is correctly enforced at evaluation time (line 535 in services/price_intelligence.py: returns None when confidence.level != 'high'). _evaluate_alert_for_product deletes stale alerts when confidence drops — good hygiene.
dashboard.py lines 62-64 double-guards confidence_level != 'high' before merging PI alerts into smart_alerts — defense in depth is appropriate given evaluate_alert already filters.

classify_data_quality has a small edge case: unit_confidence value not in any of the good/fair/poor sets falls through to 'fair' (line 93). Intentional but worth asserting with a test for unknown label future-proofing.

_analytic_observations treats missing data_quality_flag as 'good' (services/price_intelligence.py:315). Pre-DSS records without the flag will be counted as good — safe for the DSS rollout but may hide quality issues for very old records; a one-time migration to back-classify existing history could be considered.

Recommendation message for high+alert uses evaluate_alert's 'High likelihood you are paying above…' phrasing (price_intelligence.py:568-573) — confirmed non-accusatory and probabilistic. 'overpaying' never appears anywhere in the response surface area tested.
